symptom: After a provider validation failure, correcting or removing the API connection did not clear the red validation state; the failure returned after restart and could remain in the recent task list.
direct_cause: The failed adapter run wrote model-catalog.json meta.adapter.state=failed/runId/modes and provider-adapters.json retained the terminal run, while credential clear, connection deletion, and connection-scope updates only changed catalog credentials/vendors/models and never invalidated those durable projections.
class_root: Connection source state and validation projections were persisted by separate stores without a shared invalidation boundary, so deleting or replacing a source could not revoke the old validation lease.
affected_population: Users recovering a failed custom or relay provider validation
Users disconnecting or deleting a provider after a failed validation
Users reopening the model settings after a failed validation
entry_points: provider-adapter durable run and revision store
invariants: A vendor connection scope change invalidates transient adapter validation metadata at the catalog write boundary while retaining any previously published revision.
Clearing or disabling a vendor credential invalidates failed/testing/repairing/partial adapter metadata and removes its durable provider-adapter runs and revisions.
Deleting a vendor lineage removes its durable provider-adapter runs and revisions together with catalog vendors, models, mappings, and credentials.
Invalidation removes the runId lease so an in-flight old validation cannot write its stale result back after the user changes the connection.
Historical certification ledgers remain audit evidence; only the user-facing adapter run/revision projections are revoked.
generality_proof: All renderer and main-process catalog writes converge on catalogStore applyVendorUpsert/applyApiKeyUpsert/mutateCatalog; all provider-adapter run and revision persistence converges on ProviderAdapterStore, so future vendor cards, import paths, retries, and transactional writers inherit the same invalidation behavior.

same_class_scan.finding: model-catalog.json vendors/models/mappings/apiKeysByVendor; fixed at vendor scope, credential, delete, and transaction boundaries.
provider-adapters.json runs/revisions; fixed by deleting projections for invalidated vendor keys.
integration-certification/operations.json is an append-only submission/audit ledger, not a current UI validation projection; retained intentionally for reconciliation evidence.
integration session persistence is scoped to explicit session handoff and does not own the VendorConnectionNotice or adapter failure state; no stale current projection found.
lastKnown is process memory only and is already invalidated by nomi-model-catalog-changed; not the restart-persistent source.

recurrence.reason: The same source/projection split can recur for another vendor card, credential writer, import path, or adapter revision unless invalidation is enforced at the shared catalog and adapter stores.
same_class_scan: Scanned catalogStore public and transactional vendor/key/model/mapping writers and all renderer mutation wrappers.
Scanned provider-adapter run/revision persistence and integration certification ledgers for vendor-keyed validation records.
Scanned onboarding health snapshot and model settings readers; confirmed UI reads catalog adapter metadata and provider-adapter task projections after restart.

prevention.invariant: A source mutation revokes its transient validation projections before the next read can present them as current.
prevention.failure_mode: Old failed state is either removed/reset to unverified or rejected by the removed runId lease; unrelated vendors and append-only audit evidence remain intact.
prevention.strategy: Keep source mutation ownership in catalogStore, use one adapter-store cleanup primitive, and cover restart-shaped disk reads with a regression test.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old writes were updated in place at their shared boundaries; no parallel invalidation implementation remains.

migration: Existing failed catalog metadata is repaired when the user clears/disables the credential, changes the connection scope, or deletes the vendor. Existing append-only certification ledgers are retained for reconciliation history.
residual_risks: A failed record from a vendor that is never edited remains visible until the user changes or removes that connection; it is still actionable current state rather than an orphaned projection.
This zero-cost walk does not call a paid provider or expose a real API key.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The fix uses existing filesystem and catalog/adapter stores; no dependency changes.

internal_only_reason: This repair concerns Nomi-owned filesystem projections and invalidation semantics; no external provider contract defines when local validation records become stale.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Revoke transient adapter metadata whenever a vendor connection, credential, or lineage is changed.
Delete durable adapter runs and revisions for invalidated vendor keys.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: public and transactional vendor/key mutation APIs
same_class_entry_points.evidence: All catalog write paths call the shared invalidation and durable cleanup primitives.
The store exposes one vendor-key cleanup primitive used by catalog boundaries.
